Dr. '''Eric 'Davis' Earle''' (died 24 December 2016) was a Canadian [[nuclear physicist]]. A [[Rhodes Scholarship|Rhodes Scholar]], he worked at [[Chalk River Laboratories|Chalk River]] and helped organize [[Sudbury Neutrino Observatory]] as part of the project team whose director, [[Arthur B. McDonald]], won the 2015 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref name=telegram>Pennell, Josh. ''The Telegram'' (St John's, Nfld). 2015-10-22 [http://www.thetelegram.com/News/Local/2015-10-22/article-4318926/Newfoundlander-helps-win-Nobel-Prize-for-physics/1 Newfoundlander helps win Nobel Prize for physics] accessed: 25 November 2015].</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbncompass.ca/news/local/2017/1/11/carbonear-physicist-davis-earle-dead-at-79.html|title=Carbonear physicist Davis Earle dead at 79|work=cbncompass.ca|accessdate=12 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112220735/http://www.cbncompass.ca/news/local/2017/1/11/carbonear-physicist-davis-earle-dead-at-79.html|archive-date=12 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He received an honorary doctor of science degree from [[Memorial University of Newfoundland]] in 2004 <ref name=telegram />

== Early life ==

Davis was son of Mildred and Guy Earle, born November 26, 1937, and raised in [[Carbonear]], [[Newfoundland and Labrador|Newfoundland]]. His father was the final captain of the [[SS Kyle]] and part-owner of the Earle Freighting Service.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Davis Earle (1937-2016) – A Life Well Lived|url=http://www.asecondlook.info/science/2017-davis-earle.htm|website=www.asecondlook.info|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> Davis said “My father tried to get me to join him in the codfish business in Carbonear, but I didn’t want to go work with my father at 20. I thought I needed to see a bit of Canada,” <ref name="telegram" /> a goal that stuck with him throughout his life. Davis got his bachelor's of science degree at Memorial University, a master's degree at the University of British Columbia. In 1959 he became a  Rhodes Scholar and completed his doctorate studies at Oxford in 1964.<ref name="telegram" />
